title: QBR - Lumos Retail Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, upcoming roadmap alignment and next steps for a pilot of Redwood Dedicated for peak holiday traffic.
topics: Usage and cost breakdown (embeddings vs generations)
Roadmap alignment: Dedicated vs Hosted and Private options
Optimization opportunities: batching, prefix caching, quantization
transcript:
[00:00] Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; this is the Lumos QBR, we've got about 45 minutes on the agenda. Jordan and Samir are here from Redwood.
[00:12] Nina Patel: Hi all, thanks. Scheduling was brutal but glad we're here.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Quick agenda — usage, cost, incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps.
[00:25] Marco Silva: Sounds good. Nina, quick note, we had an uptick in token usage during the spring campaign, 3x over baseline.
[00:31] Nina Patel: Right, Marco; most of that was embeddings for personalization plus some long-form generation testing.
[00:40] Samir Desai: OK, can you remind us of the current split you see? I have the usage report open but numbers sometimes differ.
[00:47] Emma Torres: We have roughly 60% embedding units, 35% generation tokens, and 5% other. The embedding spike was the big cost driver last month.
[00:57] Alicia Park: That aligns with what Jordan shared in the dashboard export. On cost, we see the embeddings pricing impact — have you enabled the caching on prefix for recommendations?
[01:08] Marco Silva: We turned on a basic cache, but not the full KV-level prefix cache; our SREs were worried about cache invalidation complexity.
[01:15] Samir Desai: There's a lightweight prefix caching option that addresses TTL invalidation — it's been helpful for other retail customers. We can share the config.
[01:25] Nina Patel: Yes please, that would be great. Also we tried a 4-bit quantized model variant for inference and saw lower latency but some quality drift on product descriptions.
[01:36] Jordan Lee: Expected tradeoff. We have model profiles that recommend quantization only for certain sequences; Samir can run a quick eval on your prompt set to show impact.
[01:45] Jason Wu: On reliability, we had two incidents in March — a 10-minute degradation during the nightly batch job and a separate 4-minute KV cache eviction race. Emma, do you want to add?
[01:56] Emma Torres: The first was a regional pod autoscaling hiccup; we hit a cold start for a new Dedicated-like instance on the hosted tier. The team mitigated but it did violate our internal SLO for that batch pipeline.
[02:10] Samir Desai: We captured traces in the console — the autoscaler bias produced a short queue. We can propose a policy change: pre-warm for scheduled jobs or set a different scaling threshold.
[02:20] Marco Silva: Pre-warm sounds fine, but we need controls so costs don't balloon with pre-warmed capacity.
[02:28] Jordan Lee: We can model that for you — show dollars vs latency gains. I'll send a cost-modeling spreadsheet.
[02:35] Nina Patel: On the Dedicated vs Hosted question: our holiday peak is non-negotiable — we need predictable throughput. We're evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity for November–December.
[02:46] Alicia Park: That makes sense. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; we can offer a seasonal reserved plan or bursting policies to reduce commit.
[02:55] Jason Wu: What about VPC/private for compliance? Some of our partners require data residency controls.
[03:01] Samir Desai: We offer Redwood Private with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. For on-prem air-gapped, that's a longer lead but possible.
[03:10] Emma Torres: What's the SOC 2 status? We need audit logs and RBAC for our SOC team.
[03:14] Jordan Lee: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II is current; audit logs and RBAC are supported. We can share the security pack.
[03:21] Marco Silva: Great — please send that. Also we need a list of APIs that write logs to our SIEM.
[03:28] Samir Desai: We have API hooks and can export to syslog/CloudWatch. I'll include typical configurations.
[03:35] Nina Patel: Back to optimization: can you walk through the batching and KV cache best practices?
[03:40] Samir Desai: Sure. For high QPS embedding workloads, we recommend batching with a max latency budget of 50–80ms; continuous batching in the runtime will aggregate small requests. Also enable KV prefix cache for repeated prefixes (search sessions), set TTL 5–15 mins depending on churn.
[03:55] Marco Silva: Will batching add extra latency for cold requests?
[03:59] Samir Desai: Slightly but overall p99 improves. You can set per-route latency SLOs so critical pathways bypass batching.
[04:07] Jason Wu: We need an action item to map our critical routes.
[04:10] Alicia Park: Noted.
[04:12] [06:20] — (skipping middle of call for brevity)
[06:22] Nina Patel: On roadmap, we want alignment on three things: 1) pilot Dedicated for holiday peak, 2) run an eval for model quantization impact, 3) finalize SSO/KMS setup for production.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: We'll support all three — suggest timeline: Dedicated pilot kickoff in 6 weeks, quantization eval in 2 weeks, SSO/KMS handoff next week with your security team.
[06:44] Emma Torres: SSO is urgent — our audit is next month.
[06:48] Samir Desai: We'll get the SSO doc and implementation checklist today; I'll book a technical handoff with Emma and Marco.
[06:56] Marco Silva: For Dedicated pilot, what does pricing look like for seasonal reserved capacity?
[07:01] Jordan Lee: We'll propose two options: a committed seasonal block (lower unit cost) or a burstable model with a baseline commit and paid burst. We'll send the spreadsheet.
[07:11] Nina Patel: Also please include a failover plan — if Dedicated doesn't meet latency SLOs, can we fail back to hosted?
[07:18] Samir Desai: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to hosted model variants; we can test the failover in the pilot.
[07:24] Jason Wu: Any competitor discussions? We ran a quick eval against Anthropic last month for chat quality. Realistically, the deciding factors are cost + latency for us.
[07:35] Alicia Park: Understood. We'll include a comparative note but focus on cost modeling.
[07:40] Jordan Lee: Next steps recap and owners follow.
[07:45] [47:30] Alicia Park: OK let's recap — Jordan, send cost modeling spreadsheet and Dedicated proposal; Samir, send caching config and quantization eval plan; Jordan/Security team, send SOC2 pack and SSO checklist; Nina/Customer, align calendar for pilot kickoff in 6 weeks.
[07:58] Nina Patel: Thanks everyone.
[08:01] Marco Silva: Thanks, good meeting.
[08:05] [END]
